record_scope_definition: Each function record identifies a complete original assembly range and its hash. This pins evidence; it does not claim full source reconstruction or runtime integration. Per-function port coverage and unsupported boundaries are described alongside each record and in NOTES.md.
source_reconstruction_scope: Renderer-independent projection of an already decoded Character template selection into a CharacterTable row and ClassID/ClassName. This does not reproduce cache binary readers, RNG selection, 224-property resolution, class formulas, actor construction, or runtime integration.
caller_facts: Four source MGP records `_prim_tmp_ambusher01` through `_prim_tmp_ambusher04` use `char_template_pydata=Charater_Templates` and `char_template=GothicusCrypt_Ghosts`.
The editor-only `_templateName=MonsterCommonType1` is not the runtime CharacterTable property key; the source records do not author `charpropsname`.
The cached template has ordered CharInfo slots [35, 35, 35, 35, 37]. Duplicate IDs are retained as distinct authored slots.
CharacterTable row 35 is Crypt_Ghost and row 37 is Crypt_Ghost_RE; each has ClassID 18, which maps to class row BaseMonster.
Both selected property rows also use AI row 68, animation-table row 24, and model-file row 44. Their only differing raw CharacterProperties field is RespawnTime at field index 11 (0 versus 5120).
A source-selected template slot is a required caller input. The exact per-actor selection is unresolved without the original RNG state and actor initialization call order.
unsupported: This kernel does not decode the original binary tables; its Catalog must preserve CharacterTable row order and the original template slots.
The original random draw and its per-actor seed/call-order effects are not reproduced. No default variant is selected.
The kernel does not resolve the 224 default/type/base/gear/saved property fields, evaluate ClassID formulas, instantiate Character objects, or integrate into the renderer/actor factory.
MGP editor template inheritance/asset placement semantics beyond the observed exact runtime key are not reconstructed.
